Valley of Charashim
KAR-uh-shim
proper noun
Hebrew Ge Charashim, “the valley of craftsmen”; a valley near Lod and Ono, inhabited by craftsmen; also called the valley of craftsmen after the exile.

Biblical Definition

The valley of Charashim, “the valley of craftsmen,” was a place near Lod and Ono, so named because its inhabitants were artificers and skilled workmen: “Joab, the father of the valley of Charashim; for they were craftsmen” (1Ch 4:14). After the exile the returning Benjamites dwelt there again, at Lod, Ono, and the valley of craftsmen. The valley preaches the dignity of honest craft and the place of the skilled hand in the purposes of God. Scripture does not despise the labour of the craftsman; the LORD Himself filled Bezaleel and Aholiab with the Spirit of God in wisdom and understanding to work all manner of cunning work for the tabernacle, and the Lord Jesus laboured as a carpenter in Nazareth. The valley of the craftsmen honours those who work faithfully with their hands, and reminds the church that God is glorified not only in the pulpit and the field but at the bench and the forge. Every lawful calling, wrought skilfully and unto the Lord, is a service to Him; whatsoever the hand findeth to do is to be done with the might, as unto the LORD and not unto men. The valley of craftsmen bids the workman labour heartily at his trade, knowing that of the Lord he shall receive the reward, for he serves the Lord Christ.

Webster 1828 Definition

“The valley of craftsmen” near Lod, home of skilled workmen (1Ch 4:14); a witness to the dignity of honest craft and labour done skilfully unto the Lord.

Modern Corruption

“The valley of craftsmen” near Lod; it recovers the dignity of honest craft and labour done skilfully unto the Lord.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A valley of workmen raises no modern quarrel. Its name honours the craftsmen who dwelt there, and turns the mind to the dignity of skilled and honest labour.

The principle to recover is the dignity of honest craft unto the Lord. Scripture does not despise the craftsman’s labour; God filled Bezaleel and Aholiab with the Spirit for cunning work on the tabernacle, and the Lord Jesus laboured as a carpenter. God is glorified at the bench and the forge as in the pulpit and the field. Every lawful calling, wrought skilfully unto the Lord, is service to Him; whatsoever the hand findeth to do, do it with the might, as unto the LORD, for of Him is the reward.
